You say the word sneakers out loud, and ten minutes later your whole feed is sneakers.
So, is Instagram listening to you?
Its boss, Adam Mosseri, said in 2025 that secretly recording everyone would drain your battery and light up your microphone indicator.
And honestly, it doesn't need to.
Every like, save, share and comment tells Instagram what you're into.
Instagram says there isn't one single algorithm, just lots of small systems, each one guessing what you'll like.
One of them even predicts whether you'll stop and stare at a post for a few seconds.
If lots of people are loving something right now, Instagram can test it on you too, especially in Explore.
Advertisers can also share which of their websites you visited, so that shoe shop you browsed last week follows you home.
And your memory helps: you scroll past a hundred ads, then only remember the one that matched your chat.
So no, it's not a mind reader.
Which makes you wonder what your thumb has been saying all day.
